title: The inline Apigee X proxy for Vertex AI with AI Guard: the policy flow, what it extracts, when it blocks, and what passes unscanned

prose.text: The inline proxy is a single Apigee X bundle that fronts Vertex AI generateContent and carries its scanning policies itself; the reusable variant is [[ai-security.ai-guard.integrations.google-apigee-sharedflow]]. {{flow}}

prose.label: What is scanned.
prose.text: {{prompt-extraction}} {{no-text-passes}} The README says other dialects are scanned raw {{divergence:non-gemini-bodies}}. {{response-extraction}} {{scan-body}} {{api-transaction-id}} {{no-streaming}}

checks.do: That callers send Gemini-shaped bodies with text parts; a JSON body with no contents text, or only system instructions or images, is forwarded to Vertex unscanned.
Whether aiguard_policy_id is set in the aiguard-config KVM; a stale ID blocks every request with scan_detail "Policy not found", and a KVM change takes up to 300 s to apply.

flow.statement: The proxy listens on base path `/vertex` and targets Vertex AI `generateContent` in `us-central1` for the KVM's project and model; its request PreFlow scans the prompt (direction IN) and its response PostFlow scans the answer (direction OUT), each with a ServiceCallout to AI Guard.

quotes: <!-- Step 5: Call AI Guard (direction=IN). Auto-resolve unless a policy id
<!-- Step 10: Call AI Guard (direction=OUT), same endpoint choice as step 5 -->

kvm.statement: Configuration comes from the environment-scoped encrypted KVM `aiguard-config`: `aiguard_api_key`, `aiguard_cloud`, `aiguard_policy_id` (optional), `vertex_project` and `vertex_model`, cached for 300 seconds.

quotes: Reads configuration from the env-scoped encrypted KVM `aiguard-config`
aiguard_policy_id is optional and normally absent

endpoint.statement: Each leg calls `https://api.{cloud}.zseclipse.net/v1/detection/resolve-and-execute-policy` when no policy ID is configured and `/v1/detection/execute-policy` when one is, with the key as a Bearer token; the prompt callout times out after 5000 ms and the response callout after 6000 ms.

policy-id-from-kvm.statement: The policy ID comes only from the KVM and is converted with parseInt; a caller cannot choose a policy per request (an earlier revision honoured an `X-AIGuard-Policy` header).

quotes: The policy id is **not** overridable per request. An earlier revision honoured an
`X-AIGuard-Policy` header, which let any caller name a policy that does not

resolve-ignores-policy-id.statement: The example's architecture note says resolve-and-execute-policy ignores a `policyId` in the body without an error and applies the key's own policy, which is why a pinned ID is routed to execute-policy instead.

quotes: The two endpoints need separate callouts because **`resolve-and-execute-policy`
ignores `policyId` outright** — it does not error on an id it cannot use, it
resolves the key's own policy and answers normally.

Auto-resolve unless a policy id
           is pinned; resolve-and-execute-policy ignores policyId outright.

prompt-extraction.statement: The prompt script concatenates the text of every part of every `contents` entry, of any role, with no separator; the raw body is scanned only when parsing or walking it throws (as for a body that does not parse), and when nothing is extracted it marks the prompt absent, which skips the scan and block steps.

quotes: so a turn carrying no text is never scanned — and,
just as importantly, is never blocked for lacking a verdict on nothing.
Both fall back to the raw body if it will not parse

no-text-passes.statement: A request body that parses as JSON but has no Gemini text parts (an OpenAI-, Anthropic- or MCP-shaped body, image-only parts, or only a `systemInstruction`) is forwarded to Vertex without a prompt scan.
no-text-passes.conditions: Follows from the extraction script (it walks only contents[].parts[].text) and the step conditions gating every scan and block step on aiguard.prompt.present; how Vertex then answers such a body was not examined.

response-extraction.statement: The response leg runs only for a 2xx response from the Vertex target and scans the concatenated text of every candidate's parts; a response with no text parts skips the scan and block steps.

scan-body.statement: The scan request body holds only `content`, `direction` and, when a policy ID is set in the KVM, `policyId`; the session ID the script reads from `X-Session-ID` is stored in a flow variable and not sent.

api-transaction-id.statement: Because the proxy sends no `transactionId`, the transaction ID it returns in its block headers and body is the one AI Guard put in the verdict, not one the gateway chose.
api-transaction-id.conditions: Rests on the complete payload in scan-body having no transactionId and on EV-AIGuardVerdict lifting $.transactionId from the AI Guard response into the variable the block uses; that the API generates an ID when none is sent is inferred, not stated.

no-streaming.statement: The proxy handles synchronous generateContent only: `streamGenerateContent`, tool calls and other dialects are left to the SharedFlow, and block messages carry no detector names.

quotes: **No streaming.** `streamGenerateContent` is not handled; use the [SharedFlow](sharedflow).
**No detector names in the block message.**

Streaming, tool calls, and OpenAI/Anthropic/MCP request shapes are the
[SharedFlow](sharedflow)'s job.

block-rule.statement: On both legs the proxy blocks unless the scan callout returned HTTP 200 and the action is ALLOW or DETECT, so BLOCK, any other action, a 200 without an action and a non-200 all block.

quotes: Both write the same response variable so EV-AIGuardVerdict

block-body.statement: A block returns HTTP 403 with headers `x-aiguard-blocked`, `x-aiguard-severity` and `x-aiguard-transaction-id` and a JSON body giving the direction, action, severity, policy, transaction ID and the API's in-body `statusCode` and `errorMsg` as `scan_status` and `scan_detail`.

config-error.statement: With no API key in the KVM the proxy answers HTTP 500 `ZSCALER AI GUARD: NOT CONFIGURED` before any scan and does not proxy the request.

quotes: Refusing to proxy traffic that cannot be scanned.

timeout-faults.statement: A scan callout that times out or cannot connect faults the flow, so on the request leg Vertex is never called.

quotes: | scan timed out or unreachable | the flow faults; Vertex is never called |

latency.statement: Two synchronous scans sit on the critical path of each request, which the README estimates at roughly 100 to 300 ms each.

quotes: **Two scans per request** on the critical path, roughly 100–300 ms each.

Two scans per request, each a synchronous call to the AI Guard API, on the
critical path.

non-gemini-bodies.summary: What the inline proxy does with request bodies that are not in the Gemini dialect.

positions.says: The README's Limitations say OpenAI, Anthropic and MCP request shapes fall back to scanning the raw body.

quotes: **Gemini dialect only.** OpenAI, Anthropic and MCP request shapes fall back to scanning the raw body.

positions.says: The extraction script falls back to the raw body only when JSON.parse throws; valid JSON without contents yields an empty prompt and the scan is skipped.

non-gemini-bodies.impact: Those request shapes are JSON, so they are forwarded unscanned rather than scanned raw (no-text-passes); the architecture note's own wording, raw fallback only for a body that will not parse, matches the code.
